answer: One concrete defence is requiring each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can earn: creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, and misbehaviour slashes the stake. Like an ivory tower that only admits those who post collateral, an umber ledger records every stake publicly, and a violet flag marks identities whose stake was slashed, so the network can distrust them cheaply. An attacker must fund every fake identity separately, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomical.
